payload.novelty: Cross-source reconciliation shows that Project-Frankenstein's production vision line and Drive Retina's learned dictionary line carry complementary mechanisms: PF preserves cheap/deep escalation and native multimodal semantic integration; Drive preserves explicit learned centroids/replay/calibration.
payload.summary: Do not restore FrankEye wholesale. Preserve native Qwen as deep semantic vision, but add the smallest stable structured visual feature interface needed for a user-scoped MVC with prototypes/linear head, calibrated open-set routing, trusted-example admission, versioning, shadow evaluation, rollback and deterministic replay.
payload.negative_result: CIFAR-10 screenshot classification was explicitly removed as useless, and current native_vision.py is prose-returning semantic perception rather than persistent calibrated user-familiarity state.
payload.recommended_test: H1 compare compact frozen visual embedding + centroid MVC versus reproducibly exposed Qwen visual embedding + centroid MVC, if available, versus native-Qwen-only baseline on user-specific recurring classes and realistic OOD/near-neighbor negatives; measure accuracy, open-set calibration/FPR, latency, CPU/RAM, routing savings, sequential retention, update cost and replay/recovery.
